Related: Software Firm CCC Intelligent Solutions Exploring Sale: Reuters CCC’s shares fell 0.5% to $7.60 at 10:16 a.m. “With GTCR and Elliott’s experience and resources, we will continue to build on our momentum and extend our leadership,” said Githesh Ramamurthy, chairman and CEO of CCC.

item.title: Business Interruption Claims Approach $1M Average, Says Allianz
item.description: An analysis from Allianz Commercial of nearly 8,000 business interruption claims valued at $7.82 billion between 2021 and 2025 shows the average BI claim exceeded $950,000. The average cost of a business interruption claim is nearing $1 million, an upward trend that appears to have several causes. Claims frequency has been relatively steady over the last few years, but the average value of claims rose by more than 30% annually in the past two years, according to the report.

item.title: Arctic Sea Ice Continues to Shrink at a Rapid Pace: Study
item.description: Arctic sea ice is shrinking in both winter and summer, with satellite records revealing that the region’s remaining ice is becoming thinner, younger, and more vulnerable to melting, according to the NASA Earth Observatory. Researchers issued a dire warning: Despite a recent slowdown in summer losses, scientists warn that the Arctic could experience a nearly ice-free summer before 2050. In 2026, Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on September 12, covering approximately 4.6 million square kilometers (1.78 million square miles).

item.title: Stand hires former Nephila exec Landi as CFO, raises $70 Million Series C
item.description: Stand, a licensed insurance producer with a focus on insuring property in catastrophe-exposed regions, has announced the hiring of former Nephila Capital executive Tony Landi as its Chief Financial Officer, with a remit to ensure the right reinsurance capital is there to support the company as it grows. Stand has grown from $1 billion of property insured a year ago to now $10 billion and today announced the completion of a Series C fund raise that secured the company $70 million at a $1 billion valuation. We want to insure every resilient property in the world, and help make every property safe.” Stand already counts specialist insurance-linked securities investment manager Nephila Capital as one of its reinsurers and has now hired a former Nephila employee.

item.title: ACIC’s ACES Specialty Insurance Company gets approval to underwrite E&S insurance
item.description: ACES Specialty Insurance Company (ACES), a newly formed subsidiary of American Coastal Insurance Corporation (ACIC), the insurance holding company of American Coastal Insurance Company, has received a Certificate of Authority from the Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions to conduct transactions in excess and surplus (E&S) lines. ACIC initially plans to underwrite catastrophe-exposed commercial E&S property business through ACES in Florida, Texas, and South Carolina, building on AmCoastal’s experience in coastal commercial property. Brad Martz, President and Chief Executive Officer, ACIC, commented, “Receiving ACES’s Certificate of Authority is an important milestone for American Coastal and marks the start of a bold new chapter for our organization’s long-term strategy.

item.title: Marsh leans into AI growth but warns of systemic cyber exposure: CEO Doyle
item.description: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) carries systemic threats that require coordinated industry oversight as its implementation moves to an immediate operational driver across the re/insurance market, Marsh’s President and CEO John Doyle has commented. However, he warned that unchecked deployment could introduce severe, correlated risks to global markets, specifically via amplified cyber exposure. We’re particularly concerned about the potential for heightened cyber exposure from AI, and we are working with governments, insurance companies, and businesses to create awareness and resilience to this risk,” he stated.

item.title: James Winn appointed CUO and Head of Office, Brit Re – Bermuda
item.description: Brit Group Holdings Limited has appointed James Winn as Chief Underwriting Officer and Head of Office at Brit Re – Bermuda. Winn, currently Managing Director of Property Treaty at Brit in London, is expected to relocate to Bermuda towards the end of 2026, subject to the relevant approvals. Jonathan Stephenson, the current Head of Office, will hand over to Winn towards the end of the year as part of a planned transition.

item.title: Florida Congressional Candidate Says Home Ground Wires to Be Replaced After Suit
item.description: The founder of a central Florida home services company, who is running for Congress this year, said the firm will inspect and replace electrical ground wires that may not meet building code, after homeowners filed a lawsuit. A 2023 Florida law changed the statute of limitations, giving property owners and insurers seven years instead of 10 to file suit. Joe Strada, founder and part owner of Strada Services, based in Sanford, Florida, said remediation efforts are underway, although the Orlando Sentinel reported that a lawyer for the firm had earlier indicated that homes with the alleged subpar wire had not been determined.

Milliman has released Milliman Compliance Intelligence, an AI-native platform that helps insurance product teams, compliance professionals, and regulators keep pace with rapidly evolving, state-by-state requirements. “Compliance Intelligence is an early look at that future—expert judgment and machine speed working as one, so clients can bring better products to market faster.” The platform forms part of Milliman AI Solutions, which is dedicated to delivering AI-powered products and advisory services to the insurance, healthcare, and benefits markets.

item.title: Sun Life becomes Sunlife in global brand refresh
item.description: Sun Life unveiled a refreshed global brand, adopting the one-word name Sunlife , a redesigned sun globe logo and the tagline “Making life brighter.” The company said the changes reflect its expansion beyond life insurance into asset management, health and wealth, while creating a more consistent identity across its global businesses. By bringing the strength of Sunlife together under one clear global identity, we create deeper relationships, serve more of our Clients’ needs and unlock new opportunities for growth. The parent company remains Sun Life Financial Inc., trading under the ticker SLF.

item.title: The Hartford combines data and AI with technology in leadership reshuffle
item.description: The Hartford announced leadership and organizational changes effective November 2, bringing data and artificial intelligence under Chief Information Officer Shekar Pannala and adding operations to Chief Claims Officer Stephen Deane’s responsibilities. Pannala, who became CIO in March 2025, will lead the combined technology, data, and AI organization. Deane, who returned to The Hartford as chief claims officer in November 2023, will oversee both claims and operations.

item.title: French Supermarkets’ Cyber Insurance Unlikely to Cover Food Losses, Insurers Say
item.description: French supermarkets are facing millions of euros in losses after a cyberattack forced them to throw away food, in a crisis that is not typically covered by cyber insurance policies but could still lead to higher premiums in future, insurers told Reuters. Cyber insurance typically does not cover physical losses from attacks and supermarkets’ claims could be affected if they lacked the latest software updates, four insurance brokers told Reuters. If a state actor turns out to be behind the hack, it could complicate supermarkets’ insurance claims because cyber policies typically do not cover acts of war, according to a cyber underwriter, who requested anonymity as they were not authorized to speak publicly.

item.title: Report: Auto Insurance Total Loss Frequency Climbs, More Drivers Paying for Repairs
item.description: The share of auto insurance claims flagged as total losses reached 23.5% in the first half of the year, up slightly from a year earlier, a new report shows. Related: Report: Auto Claims and Repair Becoming More Complex The share of driveable vehicles declared total losses rose to 11.2%, up from 10.3% a year earlier and 6.3% in 2022. “That removes smaller claims from the population and raises the apparent severity of those that remain, not to mention exacerbating the share of total losses.” Related: JD Power: Vehicle Complexity Complicates Auto Valuation According to the report, self-pay repairs made up 26% of repair orders in the first half of 2026, up 0.5% points year-over-year.

item.title: Viewpoint: The ‘Unbundled’ Insurer Emerges in Age of AI as Value Chain Fragments
item.description: “The insurance value chain is separating into capital providers focused on investing and service firms that handle underwriting, distribution, program administration and claims.” “The insurance value chain is separating into capital providers focused on investing and service firms that handle underwriting, distribution, program administration and claims.” In 1999, insurance consultants notably predicted that would end: underwriting, distribution, administration and capital would separate, creating virtual insurance companies . The insurance value chain has been fragmenting for years, and AI is already accelerating the breakdown. Between him and the capital that stands behind the policy sits a supply chain: a retail agent, a wholesale broker, an underwriter, a licensed carrier, a reinsurance panel and, increasingly, a pension fund or a credit manager who has never heard of the contractor.

item.title: El Niño Helps Pacific Hurricane Region Set Record for Large, Lengthy Storms
item.description: The drumbeat of monster hurricanes in the Pacific has broken a record for nasty long-lasting storms east of the international date line, turbocharged by nature’s supersized El Niño, scientists said. On Tuesday, the Pacific will tie a record for most days with a hurricane spinning and is likely to break it soon after that, Klotzbach said. El Niño and warm water are boosting Pacific hurricanes Several meteorological factors have come together to supercharge the Pacific, chief among them the El Niño, Klotzbach and other hurricane researchers said.

item.title: Edison Utility Shares Drops Due to Willful Misconduct Allegations in Eaton Fire Case
item.description: Edison International shares fell over 3% on Tuesday after short seller Muddy Waters said it had uncovered new information suggesting the utility acted with “conscious” or “willful” disregard in the Eaton Fire. The investment firm said Edison could face at least $4 billion in fire-related damages, with potential liability reaching about $20 billion if a court determines the firm’s conduct amounted to willful misconduct. Muddy Waters said the utility’s Southern California Edison unit failed to fix deficiencies in a wildfire risk model despite allegedly knowing for about five years that it could not adequately account for high-wind conditions.

It’s an insecure world out there, and investors are responding by scaling up their cybersecurity spending.

item.title: Still runway to make good cat profits, but there are some worrying signs: Convergence CEO panel
item.description: At the Convergence 2026 conference in Bermuda this week, CEO’s of reinsurance companies explained that while property catastrophe rates have declined from recent generational highs they still feel there is adequacy and a runway to make good profits, albeit there are some worrying signs. It’s not all property risk, but for those people that know what they’re doing, we think there is still plenty of runway to make good profits there.” Carr, CEO of Oak Global then commented, “At Oak, what we try to do, is to take some of the emotion out of it and quantify how we think about attractive, okay, and poor markets. Ryan Mather, CEO of Ariel Re and Cathal Carr, CEO of Oak Global, both participated in the final CEO panel discussion at the event and while they still believe the business to be profitable, there was a dose of realism and caution in their words.

item.title: Artex Capital Solutions bolsters advisory team with Kenny and Hanley additions
item.description: Artex Capital Solutions, the insurance-linked securities market service provider and insurance management specialist, has bolstered its Bermuda advisory team with the addition of two new hires, in Michael Kenny and Andrew Hanley. Michael Kenny has joined as Senior Vice President and Andrew Hanley (still subject to immigration approval) is joining as Assistant Vice President, with the pair adding depth to the firm’s Capital Solutions Advisory capabilities under the leadership of Ben Wright, Managing Director, Artex Capital Solutions. They will support the continued growth of the Artex Capital Solutions Advisory team, which works to assist insurance and reinsurance market participants, and alternative capital or insurance-linked securities (ILS) market participants to establish, structure, and optimise reinsurance solutions.

item.title: Marsh CEO flags client interest in casualty sidecars, notes reinsurance market softening
item.description: Marsh clients are exploring greater use of third-party capital solutions, including sidecars for liability portfolios, as abundant reinsurance capacity and relatively benign catastrophe losses keep market conditions competitive ahead of the January 1 renewals, according to John Doyle, the firm’s President and Chief Executive Officer. Speaking on Marsh’s Q3 2026 earnings call today, Doyle said short-tail reinsurance lines remained soft, driven by “abundant capacity from both traditional reinsurers and alternative capital.” Doyle commented, “Our clients continue to explore alternative options to complement traditional strategies, including greater use of third-party capital solutions such as sidecar vehicles for their liability portfolios.” Casualty reinsurance insurance-linked securities structures are a flavour of the day, of course, with numerous carriers now exploring how vehicles such as sidecars can help them to share risks and optimise capital. We’re well positioned, and we believe we have the best reinsurance team in the market.

item.title: AM Best Revises Outlooks to Positive for AmTrust Group Insurers
item.description: AM Best has revised the outlooks to positive from stable for the members of the New York-based AmTrust Group. AM Best said the ratings of AmTrust reflect its balance sheet strength, which AM Best said it assesses as “very strong,” as well as its “adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).” The revision of AmTrust’s outlooks to positive reflects its market-leading position in the U.S. The positive outlook considers AM Best’s expectation that AmTrust Group will “continue to strengthen its position in the workers’ compensation market as well as expanding in other segments, while steadily growing surplus through organic growth,” AM Best said.

item.title: States Seek Children’s Data Protections in Character.AI Bankruptcy
item.description: Abigail Ryan, an attorney for the states, told US Bankruptcy Judge Brendan Shannon in Wilmington that the states are negotiating a settlement with Character.AI over allegations that its chatbots impersonated licensed medical professionals and exposed children to sexualized and abusive interactions. A group of 40 state attorneys general on Wednesday urged a US bankruptcy judge in Delaware to protect young users of Character.AI and keep their data safe during the AI companion company’s bankruptcy. Beyond the states’ claims, Character.AI has been sued by families who allege that its chatbots gave harmful advice, contributed to the suicides of two children, and exposed children to sexualized and bullying interactions.

item.title: GTCR and Elliott to acquire CCC in $6.1 billion deal

California is entering the most perilous stretch of its year-round fire season, when hot, arid winds roll down from the mountains and out to sea. With drying winds forecast to blow through much of the state through Saturday, Edison International’s Southern California utility and PG&E Corp.

item.title: Apple-OpenAI Judge Says He’s ‘Likely’ to Side With iPhone Maker
item.description: The judge in Apple Inc.’s high-stakes trade-secret theft case against OpenAI said he’s “highly likely” to grant the iPhone maker an injunction barring use of its proprietary information by former employees now at the artificial intelligence startup. The judge in San Jose, California, is also hearing a separate demand by OpenAI to dismiss Apple’s lawsuit entirely. Apple sued OpenAI, its hardware chief and a former iPhone hardware engineer in July, accusing them of conspiring to extract confidential information from former Apple employees related to product design, manufacturing, component technologies, testing methodologies and the company’s supply chain.

item.title: NY City Accuses Law Firm of Running Injury Claims Fraud Operation
item.description: New York City is suing a Manhattan law firm for allegedly running a multimillion dollar personal injury fraud scheme by filing as many as 15 injury claims against the city on behalf of people allegedly harmed due to roadway defects. The city accuses the law firm Asher & Associates, P.C. The city maintains that when it or other defendants have confronted Asher & Associates with the contradictory evidence, the law firm has discontinued the cases without explanation.

item.title: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI): Overview of consultation responses

item.title: Insurance-linked securities expand the horizon for impact investing: Smith, Sage Advisory
item.description: Speaking yesterday at the ILS Bermuda Convergence 2026 conference, Bob Smith, President & Co-CIO of fixed income and alternative solutions manager Sage Advisory, explained that he sees insurance-linked securities as an asset class that can expand the horizon of impact investing. “So, through the mechanism and the risk transfer mechanism offered by ILS, I think you expand the horizon for impact investing, and I think that is where the focus needs to be, because there’s a lot of money out there looking for this product, looking for this area of the market to invest in.” You can read more of the firm’s thoughts on the impact topic in this article: ILS & cat bonds show impact investing can move beyond mitigation into resilience: Sage Advisory . Smith is a strong proponent for investing into catastrophe bonds and other natural catastrophe linked insurance-linked securities, seeing them as particularly valuable diversifiers that over the long-term have also outperformed many other fixed income asset classes.

item.title: KCC estimates hurricane Isaias wind and surge insured losses at $3bn
item.description: Cotality (formerly CoreLogic), estimated that insured losses from wind and storm surge from hurricane Isaias will be in the $2 billion to $3 billion range. Catastrophe risk modelling specialist Karen Clark & Company (KCC) has provided an initial estimate for the private insurance market loss from wind and storm surge associated with recent hurricane Isaias, saying it expects the total to be $3 billion. This latest estimate for the recent hurricane impacts on the Gulf Coast can be compared to one from Verisk, which recently gave its initial industry insured loss estimate for Isaias, saying that onshore property losses from the storm could reach $2 billion .

item.title: Markel strengthens Marine & Energy Liability team in London

item.title: SCOR finds European captive insurers hold median solvency ratio of 221%
item.description: SCOR, a global reinsurance company providing risk management solutions, has published its latest analysis of Europe’s captive insurance and reinsurance market, examining financial strength, premium trends and solvency positions using year-end 2025 Solvency II data. The median solvency ratio was 221%, indicating that eligible own funds were more than twice the regulatory Solvency Capital Requirement. SCOR’s benchmarks are intended to help captive owners and insurance professionals compare their financial and solvency positions with those of similar organisations.
